newsitem.title: USA: CBS buys stake in sports web service.
newsitem.headline: CBS buys stake in sports web service.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS said it bought a 22 percent equity stake in the Internet sports service SportsLine USA in exchange for advertising, marketing and promotion on the CBS networks.

CBS Sports President Sean McManus said CBS was paying no cash for the position, although it has the option to raise its stake to 33 percent and would then inject an undisclosed amount of cash into the web service.
The five year deal was the first time that CBS has taken an equity position in an Internet company and comes just a week before CBS Sports begins broadcasting the NCAA men's basketball tournament.
CBS said it officially began its association with SportsLine during the middle of the night on Wednesday, as the CBS logo popped up on the various SportsLine pages.
McManus said the network would immediately begin to promote the web sites on all of its television sports programs.

SportsLine, based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, has about 100,000 pages of content on all major collegiate and professional sports and gets about seven million "hits" per day, according to Michael Levy, SportsLine President and Chief Executive. The service was started in 1994 by Levy, a former executive at Lexicon Corp and has received about $32 million in equity financing from various U.S. corporations, including U S West Media Group, New York Life Insurance Co and Reuters Holdings Plc's New Media Unit.

In answer to a question at a news conference, Levy said the sports web service would immediately pull all Las Vegas sports book data and analysis and would only keep odds on sporting events that were carried in daily newspapers.

The service also carries fantasy leagues, up to the minute sports scores and interviews and chats with athletes. The service charges $4.95 to $39.95 for the basic service and $19.95 to $39.95 for premium services like the fantasy leagues.
McManus said CBS will also include some sports video to the web service, but he declined to give details.
Peter Lund, President of CBS Television, told the news conference that CBS employees would be motivated "to make sure SportsLine does very well."

SportsLine currently has several large advertisers, including General Motors Corp's Oldsmobile division. Levy said that in the next few years he expected advertising to be "a major source of revenues."

Former N.Y. Jets quarterback Joe Namath, who provides analyses to SportsLine and has an equity stake as well, promised at the news conference that SportsLine would become the preeminent one in the field.
